brief.headline: You're 1.36% of their revenue — use that size to get faster payment matched by a small price cut, then line up Gulshan or Sanstar as a qualified second source

priceAsk.summary: Push for a ₹2–4/kg cut on Dextrose to land at ₹62–64/kg
priceAsk.basis: Our price sits in the market's typical band (₹66–73/kg) but above the India export benchmark (42.95 ₹/kg). They keep only 2.3% as profit, so a modest cut protects supply while we share the efficiency gain. Frame it as locking in volume: our ₹15.03 Cr annual spend is 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr revenue — a big piece they want to keep.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days instead of 30 days, in return for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹61.76 L cash freed up for us if we move to 15-day terms

brief.financialLeverage: They owe 2.25x their own cash (₹238.85 Cr total debt), so cash moves fast for them — paying 15 days early is worth real money. We're a big customer at 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr sales, giving us room to ask. But they keep only 2.3% profit on every sale, so squeezing price too hard risks hurting supply; a small cut tied to faster payment is the sweet spot. Their health score is D (21/100) — not distress, but tight enough that they'll value the cash flow and want to keep our ₹15.03 Cr annual business.

evidence.point: They keep very little profit per sale
They carry significant debt relative to equity
Our current price is market-fair but above export benchmark
evidence.figure: ₹66.48/KG vs market typical ₹66–73/kg and India export 42.95 ₹/kg

evidence.point: Cash we free up by moving to 15-day payment

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker with strong health (B, 62/100) and bigger revenue (₹2359.06 Cr) — an established dextrose supplier and a drop-in alternate; qualify them to create pricing pressure

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (₹821.13 Cr revenue, C health 57/100) with growing dextrose capacity — a credible second source to diversify risk

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore wet-miller making Dextrose ANHYDROUS (IV-fluid grade) — exact form match; confirm IP monograph certificate before switching (D health 27/100, ₹365.39 Cr revenue)

risks: Their thin 2.3% profit margin means a heavy price squeeze could damage supply stability — tie any cut to faster payment and volume commitment so it's a win for them too

Debt at 2.25x equity and D health score (21/100) signal cash tightness — watch for any delivery delays or quality slips; having Gulshan or Sanstar qualified as backup protects us if things deteriorate

We're already at the best price we pay anyone (₹66.48/KG) and the market verdict is 'fair' — so the room to cut is modest; focus the negotiation on the payment-for-discount swap and on locking multi-year volume
No other supplier is qualified yet — start the Gulshan and Sanstar audits now so we have real leverage in 90 days, not just a list of names
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership — you're our sole Dextrose source at ₹15.03 Cr a year — and we'd like to lock that in by moving to 15-day payment in exchange for a small price improvement that works for both of us.
